text: Are there any E. coli expression studies about ciprofloxacin?
I'll search GEO for E. coli expression studies related to ciprofloxacin.

## Abstract

We queried NCBI GEO for expression Series (GSE) records that link *Escherichia coli* to ciprofloxacin, to determine whether transcriptomic studies on this fluoroquinolone antibiotic exist in the public repository. Using the `geo_search` tool with `organism="Escherichia coli"` and `term="ciprofloxacin"` restricted to `entry_type=gse`, NCBI's ESearch returned a total of 37 matching Series. The service rewrote the query via MeSH to `"Escherichia coli"[Organism] AND ("ciprofloxacin"[All Fields] OR "ciprofloxacin"[MeSH Terms] OR ciprofloxacin[All Fields]) AND "gse"[Filter]`, so the count reflects that rewritten query. The response returned 10 detailed records (server-trimmed from the requested 20 due to size), spanning experiment types dominated by "Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing" and including studies on antibiotic tolerance mechanisms (purA deficiency, GuaB inhibition), stress-driven resistance emergence (sertraline-primed adaptation), antimicrobial peptide effects (BTP-001), 3D genome organization under ciprofloxacin, and time-resolved early antibiotic response. Sample counts per Series in the returned subset ranged from 4 to 64. Six of the ten shown Series carry linked PubMed identifiers. The result confirms that a substantial body of E. coli–ciprofloxacin expression data exists in GEO and identifies specific Series accessions available for reuse.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** *Escherichia coli* is a model Gram-negative bacterium widely used to study antibiotic response. Ciprofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone that inhibits DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, triggering SOS response, ROS accumulation, and downstream transcriptional remodeling. Expression profiling studies illuminate the regulatory circuits engaged during exposure, tolerance, and resistance.

**Literature Review.** Six of the ten returned Series carry linked PubMed identifiers: PMIDs 40879398 (GSE276254), 40804527 (GSE283264, GSE272161, GSE272160, GSE272159, GSE272158), 41805196 (GSE295494), 42079445 (GSE292923), and 39235234 (GSE275261). Only accession-level metadata and study summaries were retrieved; abstracts were not fetched.

**Knowledge Gap.** Before this query, it was unknown how many E. coli expression Series in GEO reference ciprofloxacin and which biological contexts they cover.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: enumerate GEO Series matching *E. coli* AND ciprofloxacin and characterize the returned subset. Expectation: multiple Series exist, given ciprofloxacin's prominence in antibiotic-tolerance research.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** GEO was chosen because it is the primary public repository for gene expression Series and is directly searchable by organism and free-text term.

**Materials.** NCBI GEO, accessed through the `geo_search` tool.

**Procedures.** One tool call:
- `geo_search(organism="Escherichia coli", term="ciprofloxacin", entry_type="gse", max_results=20)`

The server rewrote the term through MeSH; the executed query was `"Escherichia coli"[Organism] AND ("ciprofloxacin"[All Fields] OR "ciprofloxacin"[MeSH Terms] OR ciprofloxacin[All Fields]) AND "gse"[Filter]`.

**Statistical Analysis.** `total_count` (37) is the ESearch hit count for the rewritten query in the `gds` database restricted to GSE. The 10 detailed records shown are the size-capped subset returned by the server (originally 20 before trimming). No deduplication or normalization was performed; counts reflect raw ESearch output.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1.** GEO Series matching *E. coli* AND ciprofloxacin (10 detailed records returned; 37 total in ESearch).

| Accession | Title (short) | Taxon | Samples | Experiment type | PubMed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GSE309890 | Sertraline biases resistance emergence (tktA) | *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 | 6 | Expression profiling by HTS | — |
| GSE276254 | BTP-001 dual-mechanism antimicrobial peptide | *E. coli* | 51 | Expression profiling by HTS | 40879398 |
| GSE283264 | 3D organization of E. coli genome (RNA-Seq) | *E. coli* | 25 | Expression profiling by HTS | 40804527 |
| GSE272161 | 3D organization of E. coli genome (SuperSeries) | *E. coli* | 64 | Other; Expression profiling | 40804527 |
| GSE272160 | 3D organization (RedC) | *E. coli* | 4 | Other | 40804527 |
| GSE272159 | 3D organization (MicroC) | *E. coli* | 33 | Other | 40804527 |
| GSE272158 | 3D organization (HiC) | *E. coli* | 2 | Other | 40804527 |
| GSE295494 | Transcriptomic response to early antibiotic exposure | *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 | 42 | Expression profiling by HTS | 41805196 |
| GSE292923 | Effect of purA on transcriptome during ciprofloxacin treatment | *E. coli* | 4 | Expression profiling by HTS | 42079445 |
| GSE275261 | GuaB inhibition in *A. baumannii* and *E. coli* | *A. baumannii*; *E. coli* | 24 | Expression profiling by HTS | 39235234 |

**Findings.** ESearch returned 37 Series for the rewritten query. Of the 10 shown, 8 are labeled "Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing" (in whole or in part), and 6 carry at least one linked PubMed identifier. Sample counts in the returned subset range from 4 to 64. Studies directly centered on ciprofloxacin transcriptomic response include GSE292923 (purA knockout under ciprofloxacin), GSE295494 (early-exposure time course including ciprofloxacin conditions), and GSE275261 (comparative response including a ciprofloxacin arm). Others reference ciprofloxacin as an experimental condition among several antibiotics (e.g., GSE272159 includes `WT_cipro0025_MicroC` and `WT_cipro025_MicroC` samples).

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** Expression studies linking *E. coli* to ciprofloxacin are present in GEO, with 37 total Series matching the search and 10 characterized here. The objective — confirming existence and enumerating candidates — is met.

**Context.** Retrieved records span mechanistic angles including antibiotic tolerance metabolism (GSE292923), early transcriptional adaptation (GSE295494), 3D chromatin response (GSE272159), and antimicrobial peptide interactions (GSE276254).

**Limitations.** The tool reported that the response was size-capped: 10 of 20 requested records were returned in detail, and 37 total exist. Ciprofloxacin was expanded via MeSH, so hits may include Series that mention ciprofloxacin only as background rather than as an experimental condition. Sample titles were inspected to confirm ciprofloxacin usage in some Series but not all. GEO's ESearch counts every match in the `gds` filter for GSE, but the actual biological centrality of ciprofloxacin varies per Series. Processed expression values are not returned by the API and must be downloaded from the FTP directories.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** A rich set of E. coli–ciprofloxacin transcriptomic Series exists. A useful next query would page through the remaining 27 Series (`max_results=20, offset=…` is not exposed here — instead refine `term` to e.g. `"ciprofloxacin treatment"` or call `geo_series` on individual accessions such as GSE292923 or GSE295494 to inspect samples, platforms, and supplementary files.

[2] GSE309890 FTP directory — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[3] GSE276254 FTP directory — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE276nnn/GSE276254/
[4] GSE283264 FTP directory — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE283nnn/GSE283264/
[5] GSE272161 FTP directory — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272161/
[6] GSE272160 FTP directory — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272160/
[7] GSE272159 FTP directory — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272159/
[8] GSE272158 FTP directory — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE272nnn/GSE272158/
[9] GSE295494 FTP directory — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE295nnn/GSE295494/
[10] GSE292923 FTP directory — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE292nnn/GSE292923/
[11] GSE275261 FTP directory — https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE275nnn/GSE275261/
